proof_assessment.primary_case: A valid setup observation after the nominal setup deadline persists a lease/pod marker; a fresh watcher survives SSH exit255/missing status without inventing a retrieval receipt; later false setup status preserves the marker; an explicitly supplied matching retrieval receipt then triggers the original artifacts-retrieved termination and three absence confirmations.
proof_assessment.real_execution: Candidate watch, remote_status, local state transactions and locks, ensure_sync dispatch, terminate_owned and confirm_absence execute. Account/provider responses, SSH subprocess replies, process spawn and time are synthetic.

source_findings: The exact base-to-candidate patch adds a future-use note, setup_completed_for_lease and remember_worker_status, and changes only two watcher call sites. The 42 other existing callables remain AST-identical.
setup_completed_for_lease requires a nonempty string current pod ID and an exact setup_completion marker containing only the current lease name and pod ID.

remember_worker_status uses the existing change transaction, including .state.lock, a fresh state read, atomic replacement and fsync. It rejects observed lease/pod mismatch and remote lease mismatch before persisting status.

Only setup_complete is True for the bound current pod records successful setup. Missing, false and truthy non-boolean values cannot create or clear the durable completion marker. A new valid current completion can replace an obsolete marker.
A fresh watcher reads the durable marker after restart. A later missing SSH status cannot reopen the setup deadline for that same lease and pod.
Budget, balance, work deadline, provider identity/absence, three-consecutive-supervision-failure handling and verified-retrieval gates retain their prior implementation and order.
The preserved historical controller remains at the exact reviewed base hash. The candidate and patch are prospective artifacts only.
